review_reference: 2026-09-18 halfway-corpus owner-tag review: user-approved four-concept candidate manifest

concepts.name: Marina operations
concepts.relationship_contract: Include founders, controlling or principal family owners, and defining long-term operators who created, owned, developed or ran a commercial recreational marina or a marina-centred operating group. Former relationships qualify only when marina ownership or operation remains a defining source of wealth or public identity. Exclude yacht owners and berth users, yacht-club members, marina-industry advocates without an operating business, suppliers and tenants, one-off investors, shipyards without a marina business, and waterfront developments where a marina is merely an incidental amenity.

semantic_contract.membership: The owner founded, controlled, principally owned, developed or held a defining long-term operating mandate in a commercial recreational marina or marina-centred operating group. Former relationships qualify only when marina ownership or operation remains a defining source of wealth or public identity.
semantic_contract.exclusions: Exclude yacht owners and berth users, yacht-club members, marina-industry advocates without an operating business, suppliers and tenants, one-off investors, shipyards without a marina business, and waterfront developments where a marina is merely an incidental amenity.
semantic_contract.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Marina operations should see owners whose business identity includes creating, controlling or operating marinas, not a general collection of people associated with yachts, waterfront property or marine tourism.

concepts.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Marina operations should see owners whose business identity includes creating, controlling or operating marinas, not a general collection of people associated with yachts, waterfront property or marine tourism.
concepts.known_for_basis: Every reviewed member has a dossier-supported founder, ownership or sustained operating relationship to a named marina or marina group. The marina activity is a durable business platform or a former-but-defining part of the owner's wealth and public identity.
concepts.existing_active_review: No active tag isolates marina owner-operators. Maritime tourism includes charter, cruise and other vessel-based tourism, while Resort operations, Ship repair and Property developer answer different questions. The exact concept survives as inactive tag_3493, so registration must report that lifecycle record for deliberate reactivation review instead of allocating a duplicate ID.
concepts.broader_tag_review: Shipping and Maritime or Hospitality classifications are reporting fields rather than literal browse tags. Maritime tourism is already broad and does not consistently distinguish marina infrastructure and operations from charter or cruise businesses.
concepts.facet_review: Marine-services, recreational-boating and travel-hospitality facets preserve context but are not user-facing click-through relationships. A literal marina cohort answers a distinct and especially relevant owner-comparison question.
concepts.dossier_metadata_review: The concept is not a transaction, strategy or one-owner asset note. Sixteen independently researched dossiers satisfy the same repeatable ownership-and-operations contract across multiple countries and business models.
concepts.information_value: The current reviewed cohort contains 16 records and should remain within the preferred range as the remaining corpus is researched. It lets users compare the people behind marina platforms, a precise yacht-adjacent relationship obscured by broader hospitality, property and maritime tags.

concepts.name: Private healthcare providers
concepts.relationship_contract: Include founders, controlling or principal family owners, and defining long-term owner-operators of businesses that directly deliver patient or residential care through hospitals, clinics, medical centres, home-health services, nursing facilities, assisted living or senior-care networks. Former businesses qualify only when they remain the defining wealth platform. Exclude pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical-device manufacturers; insurers or managed-care businesses without material provider operations; healthcare software; pure investors; property-only senior housing; charitable involvement; hospital-board service; and clinicians whose evidence establishes practice but not a provider business.

semantic_contract.membership: The owner founded, controlled, principally owned or held a defining long-term operating mandate in a business that directly delivers patient or residential care through hospitals, clinics, medical centres, home-health services, nursing facilities, assisted living or senior-care networks. Former businesses qualify only when they remain a defining wealth platform.
semantic_contract.exclusions: Exclude pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical-device manufacturers; insurers or managed-care businesses without material provider operations; healthcare software; pure investors; property-only senior housing; charitable involvement; hospital-board service; and clinicians whose evidence establishes practice but not a provider business.
semantic_contract.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Private healthcare providers should see owners who built, control or operate organisations delivering direct medical, nursing, home-health or residential care, rather than the entire healthcare industry or every physician in the corpus.

concepts.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Private healthcare providers should see owners who built, control or operate organisations delivering direct medical, nursing, home-health or residential care, rather than the entire healthcare industry or every physician in the corpus.
concepts.known_for_basis: The reviewed members are publicly defined by founding, owning or operating hospital, clinic, home-health or elder-care platforms. Their relationship is supported as a substantial business mandate, not inferred from a medical qualification or investment alone.
concepts.existing_active_review: The active catalogue has Medical devices, Pharmaceuticals and Physician but no direct-care provider cohort. Inactive tag_1160 Hospital & clinic operations covers a narrower facilities concept and was previously supported by only five records; the present proposal deliberately broadens the contract to include coherent senior-care and home-health operators while continuing to exclude healthcare generally.
concepts.broader_tag_review: Healthcare is already captured as a wealth and primary-industry classification and would be too broad as a literal tag. Physician answers an occupational question and excludes non-clinician owners, while Insurance, Property developer and investment tags do not identify direct-care operations.
concepts.facet_review: Hospital, clinic, healthcare-services and senior-care facets describe the domain but cannot provide the user-facing correlation between owners of direct-care businesses. A single provider tag avoids fragmenting a coherent cohort into weak facility-type labels.
concepts.dossier_metadata_review: This is a repeatable subindustry relationship across 23 dossiers, not a catalogue of individual medical specialisms, named institutions or transactions. The contract can be assessed consistently from accepted business-ownership and operating evidence.
concepts.information_value: The current reviewed cohort contains 23 records, eight of which otherwise have no active tag. It should remain near the upper end of the preferred range at corpus completion and supplies a high-interest comparison of owners whose wealth or defining mandate comes from delivering care.

concepts.name: Education & training providers
concepts.relationship_contract: Include founders, controlling or principal family owners, and defining long-term operators of commercial schools, higher-education institutions, continuing-education centres, vocational academies or professional-training providers. Former businesses qualify when they were a substantial wealth platform or defining operating mandate. Exclude donors, trustees and school-board members without ownership or operating responsibility; teachers, professors and coaches whose role does not control a provider; employers' internal training; short courses; creator-led membership communities; and software products that enable education without operating an education or training service.

semantic_contract.membership: The owner founded, controlled, principally owned or held a defining long-term operating mandate in a commercial school, higher-education institution, continuing-education centre, vocational academy or professional-training provider. Former businesses qualify when they were a substantial wealth platform or defining operating mandate.
semantic_contract.exclusions: Exclude donors, trustees and school-board members without ownership or operating responsibility; teachers, professors and coaches whose role does not control a provider; employers' internal training; short courses; creator-led membership communities; and software products that enable education without operating an education or training service.
semantic_contract.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Education & training providers should see owners who built, own or run organisations whose product is structured education or professional training, across schools, higher education and vocational provision.

concepts.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Education & training providers should see owners who built, own or run organisations whose product is structured education or professional training, across schools, higher education and vocational provision.
concepts.known_for_basis: Each reviewed owner founded, owns or exercised defining long-term operational control over an education or training provider. The relationship is commercial and institution-level rather than philanthropic, honorary or incidental.
concepts.existing_active_review: The active catalogue has no education-parent literal. Inactive concepts such as Corporate training services, Education technology, Higher-education founder and various one-institution labels fragment the same useful provider question or encode roles and delivery formats rather than the principal relationship.
concepts.broader_tag_review: Service and Technology classifications are too broad and are not user-facing literal tags. Aviation captures a sector but does not reveal that the owner's defining business is an academy, while Publishing and Digital media do not capture structured education provision.
concepts.facet_review: Education, training, online delivery and vocational specialisms remain useful facets, but facet-only treatment would leave no literal route to the coherent cross-owner provider cohort. One umbrella avoids weak school, university, corporate-training and EdTech micro-tags.
concepts.dossier_metadata_review: The proposal describes a repeatable commercial-provider relationship across nine dossiers. It does not tag qualifications, attendance, donations, internal staff development or a single course mentioned in a biography.
concepts.information_value: The current reviewed cohort contains nine records, four of which otherwise have no active tag, and is likely to finish around 15 to 20 records. It answers which owners created or operate education and training businesses without turning every educational association into taxonomy.

concepts.name: Footwear
concepts.relationship_contract: Include founders, controlling or principal family owners, and defining long-term operators whose substantial business platform centres on footwear brands, footwear manufacturing, footwear design-and-distribution or specialist footwear retail. Former relationships qualify when the footwear business remains a defining source of wealth or public identity. Exclude fashion owners whose footwear activity is incidental, retailers that merely stock shoes among unrelated categories, materials or component suppliers, short executive appointments, endorsements, one-off investments and family associations without economic ownership or a defining operating role.

semantic_contract.membership: The owner founded, controlled, principally owned or held a defining long-term operating mandate in a substantial business centred on footwear brands, footwear manufacturing, footwear design-and-distribution or specialist footwear retail. Former relationships qualify when the footwear business remains a defining source of wealth or public identity.
semantic_contract.exclusions: Exclude fashion owners whose footwear activity is incidental, retailers that merely stock shoes among unrelated categories, materials or component suppliers, short executive appointments, endorsements, one-off investments and family associations without economic ownership or a defining operating role.
semantic_contract.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Footwear should see owners known for creating, controlling or substantially operating footwear brands and businesses, regardless of whether value is captured through manufacturing, design, distribution or specialist retail.

concepts.click_through_expectation: A user clicking Footwear should see owners known for creating, controlling or substantially operating footwear brands and businesses, regardless of whether value is captured through manufacturing, design, distribution or specialist retail.
concepts.known_for_basis: The reviewed members are closely identified with substantial footwear companies such as Tod's, Ferragamo, Reebok, Nine West, Grendene, Birkenstock, Tempe, Rockport, Rainfair and U-Power. Footwear is the defining product category rather than a passing investment or minor range.
concepts.existing_active_review: Luxury goods, Multi-brand retail, Apparel manufacturing and Apparel retail cover only parts of this cross-owner product sector. Inactive Footwear manufacturing, Footwear retail, Footwear entrepreneur and Footwear executive concepts separately encode channel or role; the proposed umbrella is broader than each and deliberately treats manufacturing, brand control and specialist distribution as one coherent industry cohort.
concepts.broader_tag_review: Fashion & Retail and Manufacturing are structured industry classifications, not precise literal browse relationships. Luxury goods excludes mass-market, safety and comfort footwear, while Apparel tags do not naturally or consistently include shoes.
concepts.facet_review: Manufacturing, retail, fashion and consumer-goods facets preserve channel and sector context but cannot substitute for the literal product-industry question. The umbrella prevents the same footwear cohort being fragmented by route to market.
concepts.dossier_metadata_review: This is a stable product-industry relationship across twelve dossiers, not a collection of brand mentions, family names or career-stage descriptions. Comparable records can be evaluated from company ownership and long-term operating evidence without favouring more richly documented owners.
concepts.information_value: The current reviewed cohort contains twelve records, including three with no other active tag, and is likely to finish around 18 to 25. It creates a recognisable, high-interest consumer-brand cohort that the present catalogue splits between luxury, retail and manufacturing concepts.
